subject: Seatbelt: post-deploy telemetry sanity + KV warmup
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acme.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+acme@acme.com
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Seatbelt request for go-live (telemetry + KV warmup)

Hi Priyom,

We’re scheduled to flip traffic to the private deployment in us-west-2 tomorrow 08/21. Security and our platform team asked for a short "seatbelt" run after cutover: 2–3 hours of telemetry sampling, KV cache priming (typical request patterns), and a minimal canary to validate routing/failover.

Can Redwood run the smoke/runbook you used in staging and share a short artifact bundle with:
- KV warmup results (per-prefix hit rates, priming duration)
- Short telemetry snippets (p90/p99 for token latency, error counts)
- Any alerts and mitigation steps taken during the check

We want a lightweight, auditable bundle we can attach to the go/no-go gate.

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Singh
SRE Lead, Acme Corp
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 10:03:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Seatbelt request for go-live (telemetry + KV warmup)

Tara — thanks for the note. We can absolutely run a focused seatbelt after the cutover. Proposed plan (high level):

1) Pre-cutover: run a KV priming dry run against a staging subset (30m) to confirm cache priming profile and adjust batch sizes. (Already scheduled 14:00 PDT).
2) Cutover: route 5% canary for 20 minutes, then 30/60/100% ramp depending on telemetry.
3) Post-cutover seatbelt (2 hours):
   - Continuous telemetry extraction (p50/p90/p99 token latency, 5XX/4XX counts)
   - KV warmup: run production-shaped prefix list (attached runbook), track hit-rate/time-to-warm per prefix
   - Failure injection: circuit hb check + failover trigger validation (non-disruptive)
4) Evidence bundle: KV CSV, telemetry snippets JSON, a short runbook PDF with timestamps and any remediation notes.

Will attach the runbook we use (runbook-seatbelt.pdf) and the priming list. Karthik — I’m assigning you the KV priming execution and data collection. Laura — please own telemetry snapshots and the artifact bundle. Mina — please stand by for any on-call escalation for the first hour.

Tara, can you confirm CloudInfra will grant temporary logfile/download access for the telemetry queries (one-time scoped link)? If so we’ll include the access id in the artifact bundle.

Action owners & ETA:
- Karthik: KV priming dry run and priming script readiness by 14:00 PDT today
- Laura: telemetry query templates + retention snapshot plan by 15:00 PDT
- Priyom: coordinate execution and produce final archive within 3 hours of post-cutover seatbelt

I’ll post updates to HBSP-58329 and upload artifacts to the Drive folder linked below.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Aug 2028 14:12:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Seatbelt request for go-live (telemetry + KV warmup)

Pre-cutover dry run complete — quick status:
- Ran 30m priming against staging prefix subset (200 prefixes sampled). Warmup profile matches expected: median time to 95% hit-rate = 8.6s (target < 12s).
- Batch size defaulted to 32 tokens; increased to 48 reduced priming duration by ~14% with no latency impact during the run.
- Priming script (kv_prime_v2.sh) uploaded to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-seatbelt-readiness (see runbook-seatbelt.pdf section 3).

Notes for execution: run as non-blocking background job; collect per-prefix timestamps and aggregate to CSV for the artifact. I’ll be on the bridge at T+0 and will push priming output to priyom@redwood.ai artifact bucket.

Attachments referenced: runbook-seatbelt.pdf (sections 2–4 updated).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@acme.com>, ops+acme@acme.com
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, CloudInfra <cloudinfra@vendor.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 15:12:45 -07:00
Subject: Seatbelt execution complete — artifacts and short readout

Tara / team — quick post-deploy readout and links to artifacts from the seatbelt run after the cutover (cutover window 11:00–11:20 PDT, canary ramped to 100% at 11:55 PDT). Summary below; full artifacts attached.

Executive summary:
- KV warmup: priming completed in 42 minutes for the full prefix set. Aggregate CSV shows median time-to-95%-hit = 9.1s; per-prefix outliers flagged: 7 prefixes > 45s (investigating, likely cold storage paths). (attachment: kv-warmup-results.csv)
- Telemetry: token latency p50/p90/p99 during seatbelt: 35ms / 78ms / 240ms. Two transient 5XX spikes correlated to a misrouted health-check config which we rolled back at 12:27 PDT. (attachment: postdeploy-telemetry-snippets.json)
- Runbook: executed steps per runbook-seatbelt.pdf; documented timestamps for each step and remediation action. (attachment: runbook-seatbelt.pdf)

Notable items and remediation:
- Health-check misroute: root cause was an ingress ACL mismatch between the temporary canary router and upstream healthcheck service. We applied an ACL correction and validated failover behavior; no customer-facing errors beyond the transient spikes.
- KV outlier prefixes: Karthik has opened an investigation ticket to look at backend shard placement; non-urgent but raising for queueing.

Artifacts & links:
- Drive (artifact bundle): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-seatbelt-readiness
- HBSP-58329: execution log and timestamps uploaded (see change log entries 2028-08-21T12:28:00Z and 2028-08-21T12:45:00Z)

Attached files: runbook-seatbelt.pdf, kv-warmup-results.csv, postdeploy-telemetry-snippets.json

If you want a short 15-minute readout on the bridge I can run through the timeline and remediation steps. Otherwise we’ll keep monitoring for 24 hours and surface any follow-ups.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
